slides.title: AST 102: Cosmology
body_text: The expanding universe
Dr. Alex Morgan
slides.speaker_notes: Today we cover everything. All of it. Fourteen billion years, seventy-five minutes.

slides.title: The Doppler Shift
body_text: A source moving away: waves stretched, longer wavelength
A source moving closer: waves squeezed, shorter wavelength
Sound: a siren's pitch drops as it passes
slides.speaker_notes: Swing a buzzer on a string. Hear the pitch go up and down.

slides.title: Measuring Redshift
body_text: z = (observed wavelength - rest wavelength) / rest wavelength
For small z, speed is about z times the speed of light
Example: hydrogen-alpha, rest 656.3 nm, observed 662.9 nm, z = 0.010, about 3,000 km/s
slides.speaker_notes: Rest wavelengths come from laboratory spectra. A shifted line is a speedometer.

slides.title: Hubble's Law
body_text: v = H0 x d
Farther galaxies recede faster
d = v / H0 turns a redshift into a distance
Example: 7,000 km/s / 70 km/s/Mpc = 100 Mpc
slides.speaker_notes: Twice the distance, twice the speed.

slides.title: The Hubble Constant
body_text: H0 is about 70 km/s per megaparsec
Different methods give values from about 67 to 73
The disagreement is an active research question
slides.speaker_notes: We use 70 for round numbers. Tell students the disagreement is real and unsolved.

slides.title: Expansion of Space
body_text: Space itself stretches; galaxies are carried apart
Every galaxy sees the others receding: there is no center
Gravity holds galaxies and clusters together; they do not expand
slides.speaker_notes: Raisin bread: every raisin moves away from every other, and the farther ones move faster.

slides.title: The Age of the Universe
body_text: Run the expansion backward
Age is roughly 1 / H0, about 14 billion years for H0 = 70
Detailed measurements: 13.8 billion years
slides.speaker_notes: The oldest stars are a little younger than that, which is reassuring.

slides.title: Cosmic Microwave Background
body_text: A faint microwave glow from every direction
Released about 380,000 years after the Big Bang, when the universe became transparent
Today it matches a temperature of about 2.7 K
Tiny ripples in it are the seeds of galaxies
slides.speaker_notes: The baby picture of the universe, stretched from visible light into microwaves by expansion.

slides.title: Light Elements
body_text: The first few minutes were hot enough to fuse hydrogen into helium
Prediction: about 75 percent hydrogen, 25 percent helium by mass, a trace of lithium
Measurements in the oldest gas match
slides.speaker_notes: Three independent lines of evidence: the expansion, the microwave background, the light elements.

slides.title: Open Questions
body_text: The expansion is speeding up, attributed to dark energy
Dark energy makes up about 68 percent of the universe's energy
What dark matter and dark energy are remains unknown
slides.speaker_notes: End on honesty: we know the history well and the ingredients poorly.
